newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EL NINO THREATENS ASIAN GRAIN, OILSEEDS -OIL WORLD.
newsitem.headline: EL NINO THREATENS ASIAN GRAIN, OILSEEDS -OIL WORLD.

text.p: The development of an El Nino warm water current in the southern Pacific has increased the chance of drought across southeast Asia, Australia and India, threatening oilseeds and grain crops, Oil World said on Tuesday.
The Hamburg-based newsletter said the weather phenomenon had already been responsible for below normal rainfall in the Philippines and a delayed start to the Indian monsoon season.

El Ninos tend to cause strong winds to blow in a westerly direction from the Pacific to the Atlantic, disrupting the development of hurricaines. The last significant one occurred in late 1991 through to mid 1992, with a smaller one in 1994-1995.
"Due to El Nino, monsoon rains in India could be weaker and more erratic than usual," Oil World said, noting that an El Nino-inspired drought in 1987 caused major production losses.
Australia is facing insufficient moisture levels in the coming months -- bringing the expectation of lower grain yields.
Early estimates have suggested a 1997/98 wheat harvest of 19.2 milllion tonnes, down from 23.6 million last season.

But the latest oilseed estimates have showed the planted canola area at a record 650,000 hectares. Despite a drop in yields due to the weather, total oilseed output will be pushed to a record 2.1 million tonnes, up 0.3 million on last season.
